title: Cliff's work for Joe Davis and the spirituals
summary: During his time with Joe Davis he wrote spirituals sung with a choir.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: And then of course while Cliff was here, I guess this was during the time when he began to form his orchestra which he finally got together by 1926, Cliff also worked for Joe Davis Publishing Company, and I ran across a sheet of music at the
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

house there that he wrote while he was working for Joe Davis called "The Little Black Train" and it stated on there that it was by Reverend Cliff Jackson. "The Little Black Train" is sort of a popular spiritual I guess of the day. This had to be around 1927 or something like that because I remember having heard a recording of it and on the other side was "Your Enemies Can't Harm You So Watch Your Best Friend." I think that was also by Reverend Cliff Jackson.
Did these have vocals added to them or were they just --

Yeah, they were with choir. They were supposed to be spirituals, I suppose and "The Little Black Train" is supposed to be the death train, or whatever, you know. So Reverend Cliff Jackson -- I don't know, I haven't read anything where he ever preached but I wouldn't be a bit surprised.
He wrote those words as well as the music?
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Was he connected with Joe Davis at the time that you made that second record in '44?

No, he was connected with Joe Davis I imagine in the days when he was making the piano roll. I guess you would consider him having been quite commercial, you know when he came and he got into the field. He was, you know, by being at the publishing house there, he probably transcribed a lot of the early songs that the singers used to do. There was a Joe Davis songbook, you know, that had all the songs in it that the singers were doing in those days and I guess he transcribed the music and put it down on paper.
